claim: it is too small (relative to transactions costs) and too unpredictable (about a third of lockups end with increases in stock prices) to build a profitable investment strategy around
quote: it is too small (relative to transactions costs) and too unpredictable (about a third of lockups end with increases in stock prices) to build a profitable investment strategy around.
limitations: Practitioner substack post by an NYU finance professor, not a peer-reviewed paper; no disclosed sample/methodology behind the '2 to 5%' and 'about a third' figures (references Field & Hanka and Bradley/Jordan/Yi/Roten-style prior literature without a fresh dataset); post dated 2019-12-11, no post-2020 update found.
independent_replication: Not independently re-derived; the 'about a third of lockups end with increases' claim is the same cross-sectional-variance point independently corroborated in Gibbs & Hao 2018 (Yelp +23%, PokerTek +14%, Odimo -33% on their own respective lockup dates) -- two independent sources agree the effect is NOT uniformly negative at the single-event level even though the ex-ante population mean is negative.
impact_on_spec: This is the central skeptical/negative source for the whole iteration: an independent practitioner who has looked at the same mechanism explicitly judges it not tradeable net of transaction costs, given roughly one-third of events go the wrong way. Grounds the frozen decision rule's insistence on a real cost model (ADV-tiered spread + borrow, 2x-cost robustness) and the date-shift/random-date placebos rather than accepting a raw average CAR as sufficient evidence.

claim: the literature documents an average abnormal return of -1.5% on the lockup expiration date (Field and Hanka, 2001), returns vary significantly from firm to firm on this widely-watched date
quote: Although the literature documents an average abnormal return of -1.5% on the lockup expiration date (Field and Hanka, 2001), returns vary significantly from firm to firm on this widely-watched date.
limitations: SWFA 2014 conference-submission working paper (later published as Gibbs & Hao 2018, Journal of Banking and Finance); snapshot is a pdftotext text extraction of the working-paper PDF, not the published JBF version; sample period and exact regression tables not independently re-verified this pass beyond the abstract/introduction text extracted here.
independent_replication: Corroborates, not independently replicates, Field & Hanka (2001) -1.5% CAR; the paper's OWN contribution (informed short-seller front-running, PE-backed non-effect) is itself a single working paper, not independently replicated in this pass.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the -1.5% baseline this iteration's decision rule is sized against, and is the source of the named tail-risk counter-examples (Yelp +23%, PokerTek +14%, Odimo -33%) that motivate capping any short position at 10% of capital and requiring the placebo/2x-cost checks rather than trusting the population mean alone.

claim: Unlike VC-backed IPO stocks, PE-backed IPO stocks do not experience a negative return or trading volume jump on the lockup expiration date
quote: Unlike VC-backed IPO stocks, PE-backed IPO stocks do not experience a negative return or trading volume jump on the lockup expiration date.
limitations: Same working-paper caveat as the sibling card (gibbs_hao_field_hanka_baseline_and_variance); this iteration's event construction (SEC 424B4-confirmed IPOs plus a first-trade-date fallback) does not classify events by VC- vs PE- vs non-backed, so this finding is used only as a qualitative caveat on cross-sectional heterogeneity, not as an implemented filter.
independent_replication: Not independently re-derived; single working paper.
impact_on_spec: Explains why this iteration should not expect a uniform effect across all 424B4-confirmed IPOs; motivates the IPO-to-L momentum filter (a cheap proxy for 'which past winners insiders are most eager to sell') and the ADV-tier filter as ways of segmenting the population rather than assuming Field & Hanka's average applies to every event equally.
